lessons: The only kind that clearly held up costs far more than the account. Of the kinds the account can afford, 3 lost and 1 gave mixed results and are being tested on paper. The board has ordered the mixed ones traded with real money ahead of those paper tests, one option at a time.
Cheap contracts are far from the price and close to expiry, so they lose value fastest and the buy/sell gap takes a bigger share.
How it is sold matters as much as what is bought: the kind that held up followed the stock rule's own exit instead of a fixed target.
